shorts.title: This Spider Hunts Other Spiders 🕷️ (Meatball vs Spiders #1)
shorts.description:
This spider hunts other spiders. Portia can plan a detour route to its prey and keep going even when the prey is out of sight.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

shorts.comment: Would you let Portia live in your house? 👇 Follow for Part 2

shorts.title: Yes, It Can Actually Rain Spiders 🕷️ (Meatball vs Spiders #2)
shorts.description:
Spiders can fly. No wings. In 2018, scientists showed spiders balloon on electric fields alone, with no wind at all.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Goldenrod crab spider: Mike Kerry (CC BY), CC0. creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Would you still go outside? 👇 Follow for Part 3

shorts.title: Most Brown Recluse Bites Don't Rot Your Skin 🕷️ (Meatball vs Spiders #3)
shorts.description:
Most brown recluse bites don't rot skin. Brown recluses have six eyes, in three pairs, instead of the usual eight.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Brown recluse: CC0, Thomas Koffel (CC BY), florawhite (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Has anyone ever blamed a recluse for a bite? 👇 Follow Meatball for more 🍝

shorts.title: The Spider That Fishes for Moths 🎣
shorts.description:
This spider catches moths without a web. One bolas species switches its perfume during the night to match whichever moth species is flying.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths
